smart-care.name: Smart Care
smart-care.tagline: Check your PC's health in one pass. Nothing changes until you review the results.

cleanup.name: Cleanup
cleanup.tagline: Find temporary files, caches and leftovers that are safe to remove.

protection.name: Protection
protection.tagline: See what Microsoft Defender and your firewall are doing, and run a scan.

performance.name: Performance
performance.tagline: Review what starts with Windows and what keeps your PC busy.

applications.name: Applications
applications.tagline: Uninstall apps cleanly and keep the rest up to date.

clutter.name: My Clutter
clutter.tagline: Spot large, old and duplicate files you may no longer need.

space-lens.name: Space Lens
space-lens.tagline: See what takes up space on a drive, folder by folder.

hardware.name: Hardware Health
hardware.tagline: Temperatures, drive wear, battery capacity and memory, measured.

tweaks.name: Privacy & Tweaks
tweaks.tagline: Turn off ads, telemetry and extras, with an undo for every change.

drive-organizer.name: Drive Organizer
drive-organizer.tagline: Keep each drive for its job: Windows, big games, light games and documents, scratch.

toolbox.name: Toolbox
toolbox.tagline: Install and open trusted free tools for specialist jobs.

activity.name: My Activity
activity.tagline: Every scan and action, with an undo where possible.

card.disksOk_other: {{count}} disks, all reported healthy by Windows.

user-temp.name: Your temporary files
user-temp.desc: Files apps left in your Temp folder more than a day ago. Apps recreate what they need.

thumbnail-cache.name: Thumbnail cache
thumbnail-cache.desc: Small previews of your pictures and videos. Explorer rebuilds them when needed.

crash-dumps.name: App crash dumps
crash-dumps.desc: Data saved when an app crashed. Only useful to developers.

error-reports.name: Error reports
error-reports.desc: Problem reports Windows has already sent or no longer needs.

edge-cache.name: Microsoft Edge cache
edge-cache.desc: Copies of pages and images Edge downloads again when needed. Passwords, cookies and history are not touched.

chrome-cache.name: Google Chrome cache
chrome-cache.desc: Copies of pages and images Chrome downloads again when needed. Passwords, cookies and history are not touched.

brave-cache.name: Brave cache
brave-cache.desc: Copies of pages and images Brave downloads again when needed. Passwords, cookies and history are not touched.

firefox-cache.name: Firefox cache
firefox-cache.desc: Copies of pages and images Firefox downloads again when needed. Passwords, cookies and history are not touched.

system-temp.name: Windows temporary files
system-temp.desc: Temporary files of Windows and installers, older than a day.

windows-update-cache.name: Windows Update downloads
windows-update-cache.desc: Update files Windows has already installed.

delivery-optimization.name: Delivery Optimization files
delivery-optimization.desc: Pieces of updates Windows shares with other PCs.

memory-dumps.name: System crash dumps
memory-dumps.desc: Saved after a blue screen. Keep them if you are troubleshooting crashes.

recycle-bin.name: Recycle Bin
recycle-bin.desc: Files you already deleted. Emptying it frees the space for good and can't be undone.

cleanup.needsAdmin: Needs admin rights. Cleaning it comes with the admin helper in phase 4.
cleanup.running: {{apps}} is open: files in use will be skipped.
cleanup.unreadable: Part of it can only be measured with admin rights.
cleanup.more: And {{count}} smaller items ({{size}}), removed with the rest.
cleanup.skipAdded: Added to the exclusions in Settings.
cleanup.recycleNote: Removed items go to the Recycle Bin, so you can restore them from My Activity.
cleanup.permanentNote: Permanent delete is on in Settings: removed items skip the Recycle Bin.
cleanup.confirmBinBody: The Recycle Bin holds {{size}}. Emptying it deletes those files for good. Everything else goes to the Recycle Bin as usual.
cleanup.confirmPermanentBody: Permanent delete is on in Settings, so {{size}} will be deleted without going to the Recycle Bin. This can't be undone.
cleanup.doneRecycled: {{size}} moved to the Recycle Bin. Empty it once you're sure, to get the space back.
cleanup.doneSkipped_one: {{count}} item was skipped because it is in use or already gone.
cleanup.doneSkipped_other: {{count}} items were skipped because they are in use or already gone.
cleanup.undoHint: Changed your mind? Put everything back from My Activity.
cleanup.doneQuarantine: {{size}} moved to {{path}}. That space is free now; everything stays there for 30 days and can be put back from My Activity.
cleanup.quarantineNote: Removed items go to the quarantine on your disposable drive (kept {{days}} days), or to the Recycle Bin if that drive isn't there.
cleanup.adminScanWhy: Windows temp files, the update cache and crash dumps belong to the system. Windows asks once for admin rights so the helper can read and clean them. They go to the Recycle Bin.
cleanup.adminReady: Checked with admin rights: cleaned by the admin helper, to the Recycle Bin.
cleanup.doneAdmin: {{size}} of Windows files went to the Recycle Bin.

spaceLens.pick: Choose a drive or folder to scan
spaceLens.readOnly: Space Lens only reads your drive. Nothing is changed.
spaceLens.summary: {{files}} files in {{dirs}} folders · scanned in {{seconds}} s
spaceLens.treemapLabel: Map of {{name}}: each box is a file or folder, sized by the space it uses.

activity.empty: Nothing here yet. Scans and cleanups will show up here.

kind.clutterRemoved: Files moved to the Recycle Bin

detail.scanFound: {{kind}}: threats found and handled by Defender

activity.missing_one: {{count}} was no longer in the Recycle Bin.
activity.missing_other: {{count}} were no longer in the Recycle Bin.
activity.restoreFailed_one: {{count}} couldn't be restored because a file with the same name is back in its place.
activity.restoreFailed_other: {{count}} couldn't be restored because files with the same names are back in their place.

settings.languageHint: System follows your Windows display language.
settings.deleteModeHint: With the Recycle Bin, you can undo a cleanup from My Activity.
settings.permanentWarning: Permanent delete skips the Recycle Bin: cleanups can't be undone.
settings.exclusionsHint: Cleanup never touches these files and folders.
settings.noExclusions: No exclusions yet. Use "Always skip" in a Cleanup review list.
settings.logsHint: Logs stay on this PC. Share them only if you want help with a problem.
settings.privacy: No telemetry, no account. Logs stay on this PC.
settings.quarantineHint: Items removed from your other drives go to the disposable drive's Quarantine folder for {{days}} days instead of the Recycle Bin. The space is freed at once. Off, or when that drive is missing or unhealthy: the Recycle Bin.
settings.closeToTrayHint: Closing the window keeps Scrub My Disks in the tray (it always does while a task runs, then tells you when it is done).
settings.guard: Watch for things on the wrong drive
settings.guardHint: While the app runs, it notices new games and folders and tells you if they land on the wrong drive. It never moves anything by itself.
settings.scheduleHint: Windows runs a Smart Care scan at this time and shows the score in a notification. It only scans: nothing is removed.
settings.scheduleMissing: The task is missing from Task Scheduler: pick the time again to recreate it.

errors.title: That didn't work
errors.accessDenied: Windows denied this, or it needs admin rights.
errors.unsupported: This isn't available on your version of Windows.
errors.io: A file couldn't be read or written.
errors.stale: These results are out of date. Scan again.
errors.busy: Another scan or cleanup is still running. Try again when it finishes.

performance.bootUnknown: Started {{date}} · Windows didn't record how long startup took
performance.startupHint: Turning an item off doesn't uninstall it. Turn it back on here, or undo it in My Activity.
performance.adminLocked: For all users: changing it needs admin rights (phase 4).
performance.liveNote: Updates every 2 seconds while this tab is open.
performance.tasksHint: Programs Windows runs on a schedule. Shown for information; change them in Task Scheduler.
performance.servicesHint: Programs that run in the background. Shown for information; change them in Services.
performance.adminNeeded: For all users: Windows asks for admin rights when you change it.

applications.confirmBody: Each app's own uninstaller opens, one after the other. Follow its steps. Some will ask for admin rights. You can look for leftovers afterwards.
applications.uninstallingHint: Follow the uninstaller's window. It may be behind this one.
applications.stillInstalled: Still installed: the uninstaller was cancelled, failed or is still finishing.
applications.leftoversHint: Only the app's own folder is ticked. Check anything else before removing it.
applications.leftoversDone: {{count}} items removed ({{size}}). Folders went to the Recycle Bin; registry keys were backed up. Undo in My Activity.
applications.updatesSetupBody: Scrub My Disks checks for app updates with Microsoft's WinGet module for PowerShell. It isn't part of Windows: setting it up downloads it from the PowerShell Gallery, for your account only (no admin rights).
applications.updatesSetupRunning: Setting up… This needs the internet and can take a minute.
applications.updatesNone: All your apps are up to date.
applications.updatesNetwork: Updates download from each app's publisher through winget.
applications.windowsUpdateNone: No Windows update waiting at the last check.
applications.windowsUpdateHint: From Windows' last check. Install them in Settings.

clutter.yourFolders: Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Music and Videos (wherever they are).
clutter.oldHint: Files of 10 MB or more not changed for over a year.
clutter.duplicatesHint: Files with exactly the same content. At least one copy always stays.
clutter.keepOneHint: Keeps the copy with the shortest path in each group.
clutter.remove_one: Move {{count}} item to the Recycle Bin ({{size}})
clutter.remove_other: Move {{count}} items to the Recycle Bin ({{size}})
clutter.doneBody: {{size}} moved to the Recycle Bin. Empty it once you're sure, to get the space back.
clutter.selectSome: Select files to move to the Recycle Bin

overall.good: Microsoft Defender and the firewall are on. Nothing needs your attention.
overall.warning: Protected, but something is worth a look.
overall.unknown: Microsoft Defender couldn't be read. Another antivirus may be in charge.

protection.noDefender: Microsoft Defender couldn't be read. If you use another antivirus, check it in its own app.
protection.passive: Another antivirus is in charge; Defender runs alongside it
protection.quickHint: Checks the places threats usually hide. A few minutes.
protection.fullHint: Checks every file on every drive. Can take an hour or more; you can keep using your PC.
protection.scanFound: Microsoft Defender found something and handled it. See the history below.
protection.firewallHint: The firewall blocks unwanted network connections. Each network type has its own setting.

profileHint.Domain: Work networks managed by an organization.
profileHint.Public: Cafés, stations and other shared networks.

protection.capOn: Apps can ask for access on this account.
protection.capOff: Access is turned off for all apps on this account.
protection.permissionsHint: Store apps can be allowed or blocked one by one here. Desktop apps share one switch in Windows Settings; they are listed so you can see who used what.
protection.noApps: No app has asked for this yet.

hardware.adminForCpu: Processor temperature and motherboard fans need admin rights.
hardware.helperMissing: Live sensors aren't available: the sensor helper is missing from this installation.
hardware.helperStopped: The sensor helper stopped. It needs the .NET 8 Runtime from Microsoft.
hardware.smartAdmin: Health comes from Windows. Temperature, hours of use, wear and error counters (SMART) need admin rights: Windows asks once. CrystalDiskInfo in the Toolbox shows even more.
hardware.adminSensors: Read CPU sensors with admin rights
hardware.adminSensorsWhy: Windows asks once. The sensor helper then reads the processor temperature and fans.
hardware.pawnioNeeded: Processor temperature and fans also need the free PawnIO driver, which is not installed.

status.good: Every drive is used for its job.
status.warning: Some things are on the wrong drive.

reason.bigGameOnLightDrive: A big game on {{from}}. Big games belong on {{to}}.
reason.gameOnSystemDrive: A game on the Windows drive ({{from}}). It belongs on {{to}}.
reason.gameOnDisposableDrive: A game on the disposable drive ({{from}}). It belongs on {{to}}.
reason.smallGameOnHeavyDrive: A light game on {{from}}. It would fit on {{to}} and leave room for big ones.
reason.personalFilesOnSystemDrive: A large personal file on the Windows drive ({{from}}). It belongs on {{to}}.
reason.cacheOnSystemDrive: A large tool cache on the Windows drive ({{from}}). It can live on {{to}}.
reason.maybeOnlyCopyOnDisposable: Data on the disposable drive ({{from}}), maybe the only copy. Keep a copy on {{to}}.

launcherMove.xbox: Move it with the Xbox app (guided)

method.reinstall: {{launcher}} can't move games: uninstall, then install to the new library (guided)
method.copyVerify: Copy, check, then the original goes to the Recycle Bin
method.relocateCache: Point {{variable}} to the new place, copy, check, then the old copy goes to the Recycle Bin

notice.letterChanged: The drive that was {{from}} is now {{to}}. Its role followed it.

organizer.unfinished: A move stopped before the end ({{done}} of {{total}} done, {{size}}). Nothing was lost: resume it to finish.
organizer.saveLocations: Where new apps and games are saved
organizer.allGood: Nothing is on the wrong drive.
organizer.planNote: Planning is a dry run: it only checks. Nothing moves until you confirm.
organizer.planHint: In this order. Steps marked guided are done in the launcher; the app runs the others after your OK.
organizer.estimateTotal: About {{minutes}} min in all. You can pause and resume later.

guide.steam: In Steam: Settings > Storage, pick the game, then Move and choose the library on {{target}}. Steam moves it and checks it.
guide.xbox: In Settings > Apps > Installed apps, open the game's menu, Move, and choose {{target}}.
guide.reinstall: Uninstall it in its launcher, then install it again into a library on {{target}}. Your saves usually stay in the cloud or in Documents.

organizer.nothingToRun: Nothing for the app to move
organizer.confirmBody: Each file is copied, then checked byte for byte. Only then do the originals go to the Recycle Bin of their drive. You can pause, resume after a restart, and undo from My Activity.
organizer.movingHint: You can pause: the journal keeps track, nothing is lost.
organizer.paused: Paused. Resume it from the Layout tab when you want.
organizer.stepDone: Copied, checked, original in the Recycle Bin
organizer.undoHint: Changed your mind? Undo it from My Activity.
organizer.rolesHint: Each drive is recognized by its volume ID, so a changed letter is noticed. Changing a role changes what counts as misplaced.
organizer.quarantineOn: On: what the app removes from your other drives waits here {{days}} days before it can be purged.
organizer.quarantineOff: Off, or the drive isn't available: removed items go to the Recycle Bin.
organizer.purgeQuestion: {{size}} has been in quarantine for more than {{days}} days. Delete batches automatically once they are {{days}} days old? This can't be undone.
organizer.restored_one: {{count}} item put back where it was.
organizer.restored_other: {{count}} items put back where they were.
organizer.conflicts_one: {{count}} stayed in quarantine: something new has the same name.
organizer.conflicts_other: {{count}} stayed in quarantine: something new has the same names.
organizer.scratchHint: For temporary work: exports, unzipped files. Things older than 14 days are listed here.
organizer.scratchEmpty: Nothing old in the scratch folder.

checkBad.targetRole: The target drive's role doesn't allow it, or the drive isn't connected
checkBad.freeSpace: Not enough room on the target ({{detail}} needed)
checkBad.targetFree: Something already exists at the target

admin.sessionOpen: Admin rights are on for a few minutes (no new Windows prompt).

tweaks.intro: Each change says what it does. Changes for your account apply at once; changes for the whole PC need admin rights, and a restore point is made first. Every change can be undone here or in My Activity.
tweaks.needsAdmin: For the whole PC: Windows asks for admin rights.
tweaks.setBySmd: Changed by Scrub My Disks on {{date}}
tweaks.adminNote_one: {{count}} change is for the whole PC: Windows asks for admin rights, and a restore point is made first.
tweaks.adminNote_other: {{count}} changes are for the whole PC: Windows asks for admin rights, and a restore point is made first.
tweaks.userNote: These changes are for your account only and apply at once.
tweaks.confirmAdmin: Windows will ask for admin rights. Scrub My Disks makes a System Restore point first.
tweaks.confirmApps: Removed apps can be reinstalled from the Microsoft Store. Other changes can be undone here.
tweaks.confirmUndo: You can undo each change here or in My Activity.
tweaks.restartWindows: Some changes take effect after you restart Windows.
tweaks.restartExplorerHint: Some changes show after File Explorer restarts (its windows close).

rp.recent: Windows made no new restore point because one from {{time}} is less than 24 hours old. That one covers these changes.
rp.off: System Protection is off for the system drive, so no restore point could be made.
rp.failed: No restore point could be made: {{message}}

tweaks.noPointTitle: Go on without a restore point?
tweaks.noPointBody: Nothing was changed yet. Each change can still be undone here, but a restore point is the extra safety net if Windows misbehaves.
tweaks.turnOnRestore: Turn on System Protection and go on

toolbox.network: The Toolbox uses the internet (winget) only when you install or update a tool, or check what is installed.
toolbox.loading: Asking winget what is installed (about 20 seconds)…
toolbox.wingetMissing: winget is not available. Install "App Installer" from the Microsoft Store, then try again.
toolbox.agreement: Installing a tool means you accept its license (see its website). Its installer may ask for admin rights.
